gloss: to be captivated by; to be mesmerized; to be unable to look away

definitions.gloss: to be captivated by; to be mesmerized by; to be entranced
definitions.explanation: To be so attracted or impressed by something's beauty, splendor, or remarkable quality that one cannot look away. The passive form suggests being involuntarily drawn in.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夕焼|ゆうや}け→夕焼け：05045_yuuyake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{美|うつく}しさ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{奪|うば}われた。
examples.english: I was captivated by the beauty of the sunset.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ドレス→ドレス：00037_doresu⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{奪|うば}われた。
examples.english: I was mesmerized by her in that dress.

examples.japanese: ⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず{目|め}を{奪|うば}われるほど⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{絶景|ぜっけい}→絶景：16835_zekkei⟧だった。
examples.english: It was such a breathtaking view that I couldn't help but be captivated.

notes:
IDIOM STRUCTURE:
⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧ (eyes) + ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ + ⟦{奪|うば}われる→奪う：01895_ubau⟧ (to be taken/stolen - passive)

Literally "to have one's eyes stolen" - implies something is so striking that it captures and holds your gaze involuntarily.

COMMON PATTERNS:
〜⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{奪|うば}われる - to be captivated by ~
⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず{目|め}を{奪|うば}われる - to be involuntarily captivated

USAGE:
Always positive - used for things of beauty, grandeur, or impressive quality:
- ⟦{景色|けしき}→景色：01395_keshiki⟧ (scenery)
- ⟦{美|び}→美：28891_bi⟧ (beauty)
- ⟦{芸術|げいじゅつ}→芸術：02712_geijutsu⟧ (art)
- ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧ (someone's appearance)

The passive form emphasizes that the viewer has no control - the beauty compels attention.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}とれる - to be fascinated, to gaze in admiration
- ⟦{見入|みい}る→見入る：16142_miiru⟧ - to gaze at intently
- ⟦{魅了|みりょう}される→魅了する：19016_miryousuru⟧ - to be charmed/fascinated
- ⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{奪|うば}われる→奪う：01895_ubau⟧ - to have one's heart stolen
- ⟦{目|め}を{引|ひ}く→目を引く：30622_mewohiku⟧ - to catch the eye (less intense)

REGISTER:
Slightly literary/poetic. Common in descriptive writing and when expressing admiration.
